parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no trans-specific criminal provision, document rule, screening, facility, custody or care restriction. The traveller-facing exposure runs through the sexuality statutes (up to 8 years plus lashes for same-sex conduct and marriage), which bind a trans visitor mainly if they engage in same-sex conduct or have a partner. Enforcement is documented once (a 2015 private-home arrest after a public complaint), with no later instance. Social hostility toward LGBTQ people is described as pervasive, but nothing is recorded specifically for trans people. Official posture is restrictive, and the state threatens returnees with prosecution. Resort tourism is welcoming, but the Penal Code's application there is unresolved. Thin trans-specific data, extrapolated from the criminalisation, absent recognition, absent recourse and restrictive state posture, places this in the high-risk band, at the upper end because no universal trans exposure is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: No document, marker or screening rule for trans travellers is sourced. Entry treatment of mismatched documents is an open question.
entry_documents.interaction: Sex-based provisions give no guidance on how a trans person's gender would be classified, so document friction cannot be assessed.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: One documented arrest (2015) of two men in a private home after a public complaint. Sexual-conduct statutes are the lever; no trans-specific custody rule is recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any detention would run through the sexuality statutes. Placement by sex or gender is not addressed in the record.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility or custody rule for trans people is documented. The Penal Code applies nationally; its application at resorts is unresolved.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Resorts and private tourist islands are described as welcoming and not subject to religious law, but this rests on travel guidance, not law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Resort carve-out is unverified against the national code, so the resort protection cannot be relied on as operative law.

care_services.exposure: No care restriction is documented for trans people.
care_services.interaction: No record of how care access would be handled for a visiting trans person.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The presidential statement threatens prosecution of asylum-seekers on return. Official posture at the UN is restrictive, rejecting SOGI recommendations. Officials are not documented as complicit in abuses.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No official protective measures for LGBTQ or trans people are documented as operating.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing is aimed at LGBTQ people generally and is not trans-specific.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific rule is documented. Sharia-based treatment of children born outside marriage is noted but is not trans-specific.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor would sit under the same unresolved exposures as an adult.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One 2013 stabbing of a gay blogger, not trans-specific. The UN agency reports undated hate crimes against perceived homosexual or transgender people. Online harassment and stigma are documented; reporting is discouraged.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No functioning hate-crime recourse is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Stigma discourages reporting, so visitor exposure cannot be checked against recorded outcomes.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection exists for sexual orientation or gender identity. The death-penalty status is contested; the legal analysis says it is unavailable, and executions have been suspended since 1953.
remedies_unknowns.protection: No documented remedy operates for LGBTQ or trans people.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of recourse combines with the criminal statute and state posture. Whether a visitor's documents would be believed at entry is unanswered.

anchor_checks.comparison: The 0.25-B anchor has documented extortion, detention and repeated shakedowns of trans travellers. This dossier documents no trans-specific extortion or raids, only one dated arrest, so it sits higher than 0.25-B.
The 0.35-A anchor has a universal trans-exclusion register enforced at borders. This dossier documents no trans-specific universal exposure, so it sits higher than 0.35-A.

The 0.15-A anchor has documented custodial beatings, trans-presentation arrests and a capital provision applied to presentation cases. This dossier documents none of these, and its capital position is contested, so it sits well above 0.15-A.

parsed.synthesis: The operative exposure for a trans visitor is indirect. The sexuality statutes, with restrictive state posture and pervasive LGBTQ stigma, would bite if the visitor's presentation or partner drew enforcement. The one documented arrest is dated, and no trans-specific rule governs entry, custody or care. Resort carve-outs are unverified. The record is thin on trans specifics, so the rating extrapolates from structural signals: criminalisation, no recognition, no recourse and hostile state rhetoric. That places the case in the high-risk band, not lower, because no universal trans exposure is documented.
